Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN) -- Police in Boston, Massachusetts, are searching for a man suspected in the murder of one woman and the armed robbery of two others, all of whom, they say, he may have met through their Craigslist ads for personal services. Julissa Brisman, 26, was described as "a really sweet, goofy, energetic kid." Officers discovered New York resident Julissa Brisman, 26, unconscious with multiple gunshot wounds at Boston's Copley Marriott Hotel on Tuesday night. She was transferred to Boston Medical Center, where she died shortly afterward. Police said Brisman, a model, offered massages via Craigslist, a popular online classified ad service. The confrontation between Brisman and her killer seems to have begun as an attempted robbery, police said. "It appears that there was a struggle between the victim and the suspect in the threshold of the hotel room immediately prior to the shooting," the Boston Police Department said in a statement on its Web site. Police speculate the man may also be responsible for the recent robberies of two other young women who offered personal services via Craigslist. Four days before Brisman's slaying, a 29-year-old woman was robbed at gunpoint at a Westin Hotel in Boston. Police spokesman Joe Zanola would not disclose the details of her Craigslist ad but said she and Brisman were "involved in similar professions." On Thursday night at a Holiday Inn Express in Warwick, Rhode Island, a man tied up and demanded money from a 26-year-old dancer who had posted a Craigslist advertisement, according to Warwick's police chief, Col. Stephen McCartney. The robbery was interrupted when the woman's husband entered the room. After pointing his gun at the husband, the suspect fled, according to McCartney. He said that no conclusions could be made but allowed that the incident "may be related to similar crimes occurring in the Boston area." Matthew Terhune, a photographer who met Brisman when he took pictures of her for a calendar last year, described her as "just a really sweet, goofy, energetic kid." He added that she was enrolled in Alcoholics Anonymous and was contemplating counseling fellow recovering addicts. He had been unaware of her side job as an Internet masseuse. Surveillance videos from the hotel where Brisman was murdered showed a tall, clean-cut young blond man in a black windbreaker leaving the property, said the Boston Police Department, which is asking the public's help in identifying the man. Representatives from Craigslist did not respond to a request for comment.

## Suspect in Craigslist-Linked Attacks Faced Scrutiny After Hotel Homicide, Robbery and Warwick Incident

**BOSTON —** A series of violent encounters arranged through Craigslist advertisements rattled New England in 2009, drawing intense media attention and a sprawling police investigation that ultimately focused on a young medical student accused of targeting women who advertised services online.

Authorities said the cases appeared to follow a disturbing pattern: a man allegedly contacted women through Craigslist, arranged to meet them at hotels, and then attacked or robbed them once inside. The investigation included the fatal shooting of **Julissa Brisman** at Boston’s **Copley Marriott**, the armed robbery of another woman at the **Westin Hotel** in Boston, and an attempted robbery-related incident at a **Holiday Inn Express in Warwick, Rhode Island**.

The suspect, **Philip Markoff**, was arrested in April 2009 and publicly labeled in headlines as the “Craigslist Killer,” though he had not been convicted. He later died in custody in 2010 while awaiting trial.

### Copley Marriott Homicide

The most serious case centered on the death of **Julissa Brisman**, a 25-year-old woman from New York who was found shot at the **Boston Marriott Copley Place** in April 2009.

Investigators said Brisman had advertised massage services on Craigslist and agreed to meet a client at the hotel. According to law enforcement accounts, the meeting turned violent inside her room or near the doorway, where she was shot multiple times. Hotel guests and staff reported chaos as emergency responders arrived, but Brisman later died from her injuries.

The killing prompted Boston police to examine whether Brisman’s death was connected to other crimes involving women who had placed online ads. Detectives reviewed surveillance footage, electronic communications, hotel records and Craigslist-related contacts as they searched for a suspect.

### Westin Hotel Robbery

Police also linked the investigation to a separate incident at the **Westin Copley Place Hotel** in Boston. In that case, a woman who had advertised services online reported that a man came to her hotel room, produced a gun, restrained her and robbed her.

Unlike the Copley Marriott case, the victim survived and was able to provide investigators with information about the suspect and the encounter. Authorities later said similarities between the Westin robbery and the Brisman homicide were central to their belief that the same person may have been involved.

Both cases took place in major hotels in Boston’s Back Bay, adding urgency to the investigation and raising concerns about how easily strangers could arrange private meetings through online classified ads.

### Holiday Inn Express Incident in Warwick

The investigation widened beyond Massachusetts after authorities examined an incident at a **Holiday Inn Express in Warwick, Rhode Island**. In that case, police said a woman who had advertised online was confronted by a man during a hotel meeting. The encounter was described as an attempted robbery or assault-related incident, and investigators later looked at whether it matched the same pattern seen in Boston.

Rhode Island authorities cooperated with Massachusetts investigators as they compared descriptions, surveillance images, phone records and online communications. The Warwick case became part of the broader public narrative surrounding the suspect and the alleged Craigslist-linked attacks.

### Digital Trail and Arrest

Investigators said they relied heavily on electronic evidence. The suspect allegedly used Craigslist postings to contact women, and police examined emails, phone records and computer data to trace communications. Surveillance footage from hotels and surrounding areas also played a major role.

Markoff, then a medical student at Boston University, was arrested days after Brisman’s killing. The arrest stunned classmates and the public because he appeared, outwardly, to be far removed from the violent allegations. He was engaged at the time and had no widely known public criminal profile before the case.

Authorities alleged that evidence recovered during the investigation tied him to the attacks, including items connected to the victims and materials that prosecutors said were relevant to the robberies. He pleaded not guilty to the charges.

### National Attention and Craigslist Scrutiny

The case became a national cable-news fixture, driven by the combination of a high-profile hotel killing, online classified ads, and the suspect’s background as a medical student. It also intensified scrutiny of Craigslist’s adult-services listings, which critics argued could create opportunities for exploitation and violence.

Law enforcement officials urged people arranging online meetings to take precautions, including verifying identities, meeting in public places when possible and informing others of their location. Advocates for sex workers and online-ad safety also argued that criminalization and stigma can make people less likely to report threats or seek help.

### Case Ended Before Trial

Markoff died by suicide in jail in August 2010 while awaiting trial, meaning the charges against him were never tested before a jury. Because of that, the allegations remained unresolved in court, though police and prosecutors had publicly asserted that they believed he was responsible for the linked attacks.

For the families and victims involved, the absence of a trial left painful questions unanswered. The Copley Marriott homicide, the Westin robbery and the Warwick Holiday Inn Express incident remain remembered as part of a chilling series of cases that exposed the risks of anonymous online encounters and changed the national conversation about internet-based classifieds.
